subject: prelims-polity
stem: Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes untouchability?
explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form; enforcing any disability arising from it is an offence.

optionReasoning.A: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law, not the abolition of untouchability.
optionReasoning.B: Article 17 abolishes untouchability.
optionReasoning.C: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds such as religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, but does not name untouchability.
optionReasoning.D: Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.

misconception.text: Article 15 deals with caste-based discrimination, so it looks right, but untouchability is abolished specifically by Article 17.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: On which date did the Constitution of India come into force?
explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, but it came into force on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day.

optionReasoning.A: 15 August 1947 is the date of Independence, before the Constitution existed.
optionReasoning.B: 26 November 1949 is the date of adoption, when only some provisions took effect.
optionReasoning.C: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.
optionReasoning.D: 26 January 1952 does not correspond to any constitutional milestone; the first general election was held in 1951-52.

misconception.text: Adoption and commencement are different events; 26 November 1949 is the adoption date.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Part IV-A with Article 51A, listing the Fundamental Duties.

optionReasoning.A: The 42nd Amendment inserted Part IV-A (Article 51A).
optionReasoning.B: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from the Fundamental Rights and restored several safeguards.
optionReasoning.C: The 52nd Amendment (1985) added the anti-defection provisions (Tenth Schedule).
optionReasoning.D: The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj.

misconception.text: The 44th is often linked with undoing the 42nd Amendment, but it did not introduce the Fundamental Duties.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the election of the President and the Vice-President of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The President of India is elected by an electoral college.
The Vice-President of India is elected directly by the people.
explanation: The President is elected by an electoral college of elected members of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies. The Vice-President is elected by the members of both Houses of Parliament, not directly by the people.

optionReasoning.A: Statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is not.
optionReasoning.B: Statement 2 is incorrect, so it cannot be the only correct statement.
optionReasoning.C: Statement 2 is incorrect, so both cannot be correct.
optionReasoning.D: Statement 1 is correct, so neither is wrong.

misconception.text: Because the President is chosen by an electoral college, many assume the Vice-President is chosen by direct vote; the VP is elected by an electoral college of MPs.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: What is the minimum age to be eligible for election to the Lok Sabha?
explanation: Article 84 requires a candidate for the Lok Sabha to be at least 25 years old (30 for the Rajya Sabha).

optionReasoning.A: 21 was the voting age before the 61st Amendment Act, 1988 (in force from 1989); it is not the age for Lok Sabha candidature.
optionReasoning.B: 25 years is the minimum age under Article 84.
optionReasoning.C: 30 years is the minimum age for the Rajya Sabha and the Legislative Council.
optionReasoning.D: 35 years is the minimum age for the President and Vice-President.

misconception.text: 30 is the minimum for the Rajya Sabha, which is easily confused with the Lok Sabha age.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Who presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
explanation: Under Article 108 the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting (in the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker).

optionReasoning.A: The President summons the sitting but does not preside over it.
optionReasoning.B: The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, but does not preside over a joint sitting.
optionReasoning.C: The Prime Minister leads the government but holds no presiding role in Parliament.
optionReasoning.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting.

misconception.text: The Vice-President is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, so it seems natural that the VP chairs a joint sitting; it is the Speaker who does.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The normal term of the Lok Sabha is six years.
The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution.
explanation: The Lok Sabha's normal term is five years from its first sitting, not six. The Rajya Sabha is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every second year.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Correct: statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: Six years is the term of a Rajya Sabha member, which is wrongly transferred to the Lok Sabha, so statement 1 is accepted.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the right to free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen years?
explanation: Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment Act (2002), makes free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 a Fundamental Right.

optionReasoning.A: Article 21A provides the right to education.
optionReasoning.B: Article 19 lists the freedoms such as speech and assembly.
optionReasoning.C: Article 29 protects the interests of minorities, including their culture and language.
optionReasoning.D: Article 32 is the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

misconception.text: Article 32 is the remedy for enforcing rights, so it is sometimes picked for any 'right'-based question.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: The writ of habeas corpus is issued to:
options: direct a public official to perform a public duty
quash the order of a lower court
produce a detained person before the court
question the authority under which a person holds a public office
explanation: Habeas corpus (literally 'you may have the body') requires the detaining authority to produce the person before the court so that the lawfulness of the detention can be examined.

optionReasoning.A: That describes mandamus.
optionReasoning.B: That describes certiorari, which quashes orders of lower courts or tribunals.
optionReasoning.C: Habeas corpus requires the production of the detained person before the court.
optionReasoning.D: That describes quo warranto.

misconception.text: Mandamus is also commonly described as a command, so it is confused with habeas corpus.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Consider the following statements regarding Money Bills. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A Money Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
The Rajya Sabha can reject a Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha.
explanation: Under Article 109 a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha may only make recommendations within 14 days, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject, so the Rajya Sabha cannot reject a Money Bill.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.B: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.D: Correct: neither statement is correct.

misconception.text: Money Bills are assumed to behave like ordinary Bills, which can start in either House and be rejected by the Rajya Sabha.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the power to issue writs. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Supreme Court can issue writs under Article 32 for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
A High Court can issue writs only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
explanation: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for Fundamental Rights. Article 226 gives High Courts a wider power: to issue writs for Fundamental Rights and for 'any other purpose'.

optionReasoning.A: Statement 1 is correct; statement 2 is wrong.
optionReasoning.B: Statement 2 is wrong because Article 226 is wider.
optionReasoning.C: Statement 2 is wrong, so both cannot be correct.
optionReasoning.D: Statement 1 is correct, so 'neither' is wrong.

misconception.text: People often think the High Courts' writ power mirrors the Supreme Court's; Article 226 extends beyond Fundamental Rights.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
explanation: Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) contains the Directive Principles of State Policy.

optionReasoning.A: Part III contains the Fundamental Rights.
optionReasoning.B: Part IV-A contains the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A).
optionReasoning.C: Part V deals with the Union (executive, Parliament, judiciary).
optionReasoning.D: Part IV contains the Directive Principles.

misconception.text: Part III and Part IV are adjacent and both concern citizens' welfare; Part III is the Fundamental Rights.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Governor of a State. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Governor of a State is appointed by the President.
The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
explanation: Article 155 states that the Governor is appointed by the President by warrant, and Article 156 says the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President (normally for five years).

optionReasoning.A: Statement 2 is also correct, so 1 alone is incomplete.
optionReasoning.B: Statement 1 is also correct, so 2 alone is incomplete.
optionReasoning.C: Both statements are correct (Articles 155 and 156).
optionReasoning.D: Both statements are correct, so 'neither' is wrong.

misconception.text: Fixed five-year terms make people think the Governor cannot be removed at will; Article 156 provides for pleasure of the President.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: The procedure for the impeachment of the President of India is given in which Article?
explanation: Article 61 lays down the procedure for impeaching the President for violation of the Constitution.

optionReasoning.A: Article 52 says there shall be a President of India.
optionReasoning.B: Article 61 prescribes the impeachment procedure.
optionReasoning.C: Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.
optionReasoning.D: Article 356 deals with President's Rule in a State.

misconception.text: Article 356 is often associated with presidential power, but it concerns constitutional failure in States.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by the Prime Minister.
The Comptroller and Auditor General can be removed from office in the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.
explanation: Article 148 provides that the CAG is appointed by the President by warrant, not by the Prime Minister. The CAG can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds applicable to a Supreme Court judge, which safeguards independence.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Correct: statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: The Prime Minister heads the government and is assumed to make senior appointments, but the CAG is appointed by the President.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: A National Emergency on the ground of war, external aggression or armed rebellion is proclaimed under which Article?
explanation: Article 352 empowers the President to proclaim a National Emergency on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion.

optionReasoning.A: Article 352 is the National Emergency provision.
optionReasoning.B: Article 356 provides for President's Rule when constitutional machinery fails in a State.
optionReasoning.C: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency.
optionReasoning.D: Article 365 deals with the effect of failure to comply with Union directions.

misconception.text: Article 356 is the more frequently discussed emergency article, but it is State-level.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Which of the following subjects is in the Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule?
explanation: Forests were moved from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment (1976). Defence and currency are Union subjects and police is a State subject.

optionReasoning.A: Defence is in the Union List.
optionReasoning.B: Police is in the State List.
optionReasoning.C: Forests are in the Concurrent List.
optionReasoning.D: Currency, coinage and legal tender are in the Union List.

misconception.text: Police seems like a shared responsibility, but it is a State List subject.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the basic structure doctrine. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: According to the basic structure doctrine, Parliament has no power to amend the Constitution at all.
The doctrine of the basic structure was laid down by the Supreme Court in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973).
explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Supreme Court held that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot alter its basic structure. The doctrine limits the amending power; it does not remove it.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Correct: statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: The doctrine is imagined as a ban on amendments, so statement 1 is accepted.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the lapse of Bills on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A Bill originated in the Rajya Sabha and pending there does not lapse on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
explanation: The Rajya Sabha is not dissolved, so a Bill pending there that has not been passed by the Lok Sabha survives. A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha but pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses with dissolution.

optionReasoning.A: Statement 2 is also correct.
optionReasoning.B: Statement 1 is also correct.
optionReasoning.C: Both statements are correct.
optionReasoning.D: Both statements are correct, so 'neither' is wrong.

misconception.text: It is assumed that pending Bills in the Rajya Sabha never lapse; a Lok Sabha-passed Bill pending there does lapse.

subject: prelims-polity
stem: Which of the following is a constitutional body?
explanation: The Election Commission is established by Article 324. NITI Aayog was created by a Cabinet resolution, while the NHRC and CVC are statutory bodies.

optionReasoning.A: NITI Aayog is a non-statutory body set up by an executive resolution.
optionReasoning.B: The Election Commission derives its existence from Article 324.
optionReasoning.C: The NHRC is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
optionReasoning.D: The CVC is a statutory body under the CVC Act, 2003.

subject: prelims-history
stem: The Battle of Plassey, which established the political power of the English East India Company in Bengal, was fought in which year?

optionReasoning.B: 1764 is the year of the Battle of Buxar.

subject: prelims-history
stem: Who founded the Maurya Empire?
explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE with the guidance of Kautilya, after overthrowing the Nandas.

optionReasoning.A: Ashoka was the third Mauryan ruler, famous for the Kalinga war and his edicts.
optionReasoning.B: Bindusara was Chandragupta's son and Ashoka's father.
optionReasoning.C: Brihadratha was the last Mauryan ruler, killed by Pushyamitra Shunga.
optionReasoning.D: Chandragupta Maurya was the founder.

misconception.text: Ashoka is the best-known Mauryan, so he is often credited with founding the empire.

subject: prelims-history
stem: The Dandi March of 1930 led by Mahatma Gandhi was associated with which movement?
explanation: The Dandi March (March-April 1930), in which Gandhi broke the salt law, marked the start of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

optionReasoning.A: The Dandi March began the Civil Disobedience Movement.
optionReasoning.B: The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920-22.
optionReasoning.C: The Quit India Movement was launched in 1942.
optionReasoning.D: The Khilafat Movement (1919-24) was linked to the Ottoman Caliphate issue.

subject: prelims-history
stem: The ancient treatise on statecraft, the Arthashastra, is attributed to:
explanation: The Arthashastra is attributed to Kautilya (also called Chanakya or Vishnugupta), the adviser of Chandragupta Maurya.

subject: prelims-history
stem: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885; its first session was held in Bombay under W. C. Bonnerjee.

optionReasoning.B: The INC was founded in 1885.
optionReasoning.C: 1905 was the year of the Partition of Bengal.
optionReasoning.D: 1919 saw the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

optionReasoning.B: 1935 is the year of the Government of India Act.
optionReasoning.C: The Quit India Movement was launched in 1942.
optionReasoning.D: 1946 is the year of the Cabinet Mission and naval mutiny.

subject: prelims-history

subject: prelims-history

subject: prelims-geography
stem: The Indian Standard Time is based on which longitude?
explanation: The Standard Meridian of India is 82 degrees 30 minutes E, passing near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh; IST is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT.

optionReasoning.B: IST is based on 82 degrees 30 minutes E.
optionReasoning.C: 97 degrees 25 minutes E is the easternmost longitude of India.
optionReasoning.D: 90 degrees E is not a standard meridian used for IST.

misconception.text: The extreme longitudes of the country are confused with the standard meridian.

subject: prelims-geography
stem: Which soil type is considered most suitable for growing cotton?
explanation: Black (regur) soil is rich in clay, retains moisture and is formed from basaltic rock in the Deccan, making it ideal for cotton.

optionReasoning.A: Alluvial soil is best known for rice, wheat and sugarcane.
optionReasoning.B: Red soil suits millets and pulses.
optionReasoning.C: Black soil is ideal for cotton.
optionReasoning.D: Laterite soil suits plantation crops such as cashew.

misconception.text: Alluvial soil is the most widespread and is assumed to fit every crop.

subject: prelims-geography
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Tropic of Cancer in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Odisha.
The Tropic of Cancer passes through Madhya Pradesh.
explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight States: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha lies to the south of it.

subject: prelims-geography
stem: Consider the following statements regarding rainfall in the Western Ghats and the Deccan. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The windward side of the Western Ghats receives heavy rainfall from the southwest monsoon.
The interior of the Deccan Plateau east of the Western Ghats lies in a rain shadow.
explanation: Moist southwest monsoon winds rise over the Western Ghats and shed heavy rain on the western slopes, leaving the leeward Deccan interior comparatively dry.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.

optionReasoning.C: Correct: both statements are correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: Heavy rain on the Ghats leads people to think the whole peninsula is wet.

subject: prelims-geography
stem: Which of the following rivers flows westwards through a rift valley and drains into the Arabian Sea?
explanation: The Narmada, like the Tapi, flows westward through a rift valley and ends in the Gulf of Khambhat in the Arabian Sea.

optionReasoning.A: The Mahanadi flows east into the Bay of Bengal.
optionReasoning.B: The Godavari flows east into the Bay of Bengal.
optionReasoning.C: The Krishna flows east into the Bay of Bengal.
optionReasoning.D: The Narmada flows west through a rift valley.

misconception.text: The Godavari is the biggest peninsular river, and many assume the biggest flows to the west.

subject: prelims-geography
stem: Which is the outermost (southernmost) range of the Himalayas?
explanation: The Shiwaliks are the outermost and lowest ranges of the Himalayas; the Himadri is the highest, innermost range and the Himachal (Lesser Himalaya) lies between.

optionReasoning.A: Himadri is the innermost, highest range.
optionReasoning.B: Shiwalik is the outermost range.
optionReasoning.C: Himachal is the middle range.
optionReasoning.D: The Karakoram is a trans-Himalayan range to the north.

misconception.text: Himachal sounds like the foothills of the Himalayas, but it is the middle range.

subject: prelims-geography
stem: Which is the largest coastal lagoon in India?
explanation: Chilika Lake in Odisha is the largest coastal lagoon in India. Pulicat is the second largest, Vembanad is a backwater lake in Kerala and Loktak is a freshwater lake in Manipur.

optionReasoning.A: Chilika is the largest coastal lagoon.
optionReasoning.B: Pulicat is the second largest lagoon.
optionReasoning.C: Vembanad is a large backwater lake in Kerala, not the largest lagoon.
optionReasoning.D: Loktak is an inland freshwater lake.

misconception.text: Pulicat is also a major lagoon on the east coast, so the two are confused.

subject: prelims-geography
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Sundarbans delta has been formed by the Ganga and the Brahmaputra.
In Bangladesh the main channel of the Brahmaputra is known as the Jamuna.
explanation: The Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, the largest in the world, includes the Sundarbans. In Bangladesh the Brahmaputra flows as the Jamuna before joining the Padma.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Correct: both statements are correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: Jamuna sounds like the Yamuna of India, but in Bangladesh it is the Brahmaputra.

subject: prelims-geography
stem: Consider the following statements regarding ocean currents. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Benguela Current off southwestern Africa is a warm current.
The Labrador Current is a warm current flowing along the northeast coast of North America.
explanation: The Benguela Current flows north along the southwest coast of Africa and is cold. The Labrador Current brings cold water south along the northeast coast of North America.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.B: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.D: Correct: neither statement is correct.

misconception.text: Warm currents such as the Gulf Stream are better known, so currents are assumed to be warm; both named here are cold.

subject: prelims-geography
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the retreat of the monsoon in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The southwest monsoon begins to withdraw first from northwest India.
Coastal Tamil Nadu receives much of its annual rainfall in October-December from the retreating monsoon.
explanation: The monsoon withdraws from northwest India around September and the retreating monsoon, or northeast monsoon, brings substantial rain to the Tamil Nadu coast in October-December.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Correct: both statements are correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: Tamil Nadu is thought of as dry in summer, so its main rainy season is overlooked.

subject: prelims-geography
stem: The Ten Degree Channel separates which two island groups?
options: Minicoy and the rest of Lakshadweep
explanation: The Ten Degree Channel lies along 10 degrees north and separates Little Andaman (Andaman) from Car Nicobar (Nicobar).

optionReasoning.A: The Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives.
optionReasoning.B: The Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the main Lakshadweep islands.
optionReasoning.C: The Ten Degree Channel separates Andaman and Nicobar.
optionReasoning.D: The Palk Strait separates India and Sri Lanka.

misconception.text: The numbered channels are easily confused; the Eight Degree Channel lies near Minicoy and the Maldives.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: In India, currency notes (other than the one-rupee note) are issued by:
explanation: Under the RBI Act, the Reserve Bank of India has the sole right to issue bank notes in India. Rupee coins and the one-rupee note are issued by the Government of India.

optionReasoning.A: The SBI is a commercial bank and does not issue notes.
optionReasoning.B: The RBI issues currency notes.
optionReasoning.C: The Ministry of Finance issues coins and one-rupee notes, not the other notes.
optionReasoning.D: NABARD is a development bank for agriculture and rural development.

misconception.text: The Government mints coins and issues the one-rupee note, so the Finance Ministry seems to issue all currency.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures:
options: the total income earned by a country's citizens abroad
the total value of a country's exports in a year
the government's total revenue in a year
the total market value of final goods and services produced within a country in a year
explanation: GDP is the market value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country in a period, usually a year.

optionReasoning.A: Income earned by citizens abroad enters Gross National Product, not GDP.
optionReasoning.B: Exports are only a component of GDP.
optionReasoning.C: Government revenue is a fiscal concept, not output.
optionReasoning.D: This is the definition of GDP.

misconception.text: GNP and GDP are often confused; the territory of production, not nationality, defines GDP.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: Which of the following is a direct tax?
explanation: A direct tax is paid directly by the person on whom it is levied; income tax is the standard example. GST, customs and excise duties are indirect taxes whose burden can be shifted to consumers.

optionReasoning.A: Income tax is a direct tax.
optionReasoning.B: GST is an indirect tax.
optionReasoning.C: Customs duty is an indirect tax on imports.
optionReasoning.D: Excise duty is an indirect tax on production.

misconception.text: GST is the tax people deal with most often, so it is thought to be paid directly by them.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: Inflation refers to:
options: a rise in the price of a single commodity
a fall in the general price level
a sustained rise in the general price level
an increase in the output of the economy
explanation: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level over time, which reduces the purchasing power of money.

optionReasoning.A: A rise in one price is a relative price change, not inflation.
optionReasoning.B: A fall in the general price level is deflation.
optionReasoning.C: This describes inflation.
optionReasoning.D: An increase in output is economic growth.

misconception.text: A single sharp price rise is reported as inflation in the news, but inflation refers to the general price level.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: The repo rate is the rate at which:
options: commercial banks lend to the public
the RBI borrows from commercial banks
commercial banks pay interest on savings deposits
the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
explanation: The repo rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term money to banks against government securities. The rate at which it borrows from banks is the reverse repo rate.

optionReasoning.A: That is a lending rate of banks.
optionReasoning.B: That is the reverse repo rate.
optionReasoning.C: That is the deposit rate.
optionReasoning.D: This is the repo rate.

misconception.text: Repo and reverse repo are mixed up because both involve RBI and banks.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: The financial (fiscal) year of the Government of India runs from:
explanation: India's financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March; the Union Budget is presented before the year begins.

optionReasoning.A: That is the calendar year.
optionReasoning.B: The Indian financial year is 1 April to 31 March.
optionReasoning.C: 1 July to 30 June is used in some other countries, such as Australia.
optionReasoning.D: 1 October to 30 September is used in the United States for federal budgets.

misconception.text: The calendar year is assumed to be the financial year.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Goods and Services Tax. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Goods and Services Tax replaced the income tax.
The Goods and Services Tax is a destination-based tax on consumption.
explanation: GST is a destination-based consumption tax levied on the supply of goods and services, subsuming many indirect taxes. Income tax is a direct tax on income and continues alongside it.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Correct: statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: GST is a big tax reform, so it is thought to have replaced all earlier taxes.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: Consider the following statements regarding fiscal and revenue deficits. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Fiscal deficit is the excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings.
Revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
explanation: These are the standard definitions used in the Union Budget: fiscal deficit equals total expenditure minus total receipts other than borrowings, and revenue deficit equals revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Correct: both statements are correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: The two deficits are often treated as one measure, so the separate definition of the revenue deficit in statement 2 is wrongly doubted.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is:
options: the share of a bank's deposits that it must hold in government securities
the share of a bank's deposits that it must keep with the RBI in cash
the ratio of a bank's loans to its deposits
the rate at which the RBI lends to banks
explanation: CRR is the fraction of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be maintained as cash balance with the RBI. The requirement to hold government securities is the SLR.

optionReasoning.A: This describes the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR).
optionReasoning.B: This defines the CRR.
optionReasoning.C: This is the credit-deposit ratio.
optionReasoning.D: This is the repo rate.

misconception.text: SLR and CRR are both reserve requirements, and the SLR is held in securities, not as cash with the RBI.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: Consider the following statements regarding open market operations. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: When the RBI sells government securities in the open market, it increases the liquidity in the banking system.
Open market operations involve the buying and selling of government securities by the central bank.
explanation: Open market operations are conducted by buying or selling government securities. A sale of securities by the RBI takes money out of the system, so it reduces liquidity.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Correct: statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: Selling is thought of as 'giving' something to banks, but the banks pay money to the RBI.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: Which body recommends the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) of agricultural crops to the Government of India?
options: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
explanation: The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) recommends MSPs; the Government of India announces them after approval.

optionReasoning.B: NABARD provides agricultural credit.
optionReasoning.C: The FCI procures foodgrains at MSP but does not recommend it.

misconception.text: The FCI procures at MSP, so it is assumed to determine it.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: Consider the following statements regarding per capita income and national income. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: National income is always equal to GDP at market prices.
Per capita income is obtained by dividing national income by the population.
explanation: Per capita income equals national income divided by population. National income is net national product at factor cost, which differs from GDP at market prices by depreciation, net factor income from abroad, and net indirect taxes.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Correct: statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the repo rate and the Cash Reserve Ratio. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A reduction in the repo rate generally lowers the banks' cost of borrowing from the RBI.
An increase in the CRR increases the lendable resources of banks.
explanation: A lower repo rate reduces the cost at which banks borrow from the RBI. A higher CRR forces banks to keep more cash with the RBI, which reduces the funds available for lending.

optionReasoning.B: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.

misconception.text: A higher reserve ratio is thought to strengthen banks' funds, but the cash is parked with the RBI.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: In India's money supply measures, M1 consists of:
options: M1 plus post office savings bank deposits
currency with the public plus all time deposits
currency with the public, demand deposits with banks and other deposits with the RBI
notes and coins in circulation only
explanation: M1 (narrow money) is currency with the public plus demand deposits with banks plus other deposits with the RBI. Post-office savings deposits enter broader measures.

misconception.text: Money is commonly equated with notes and coins, but M1 includes demand deposits.

subject: prelims-economy
stem: Consider the following statements regarding deflation and disinflation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Disinflation means the same thing as deflation.
Deflation is a fall in the general price level.
explanation: Deflation is a decline in the general price level. Disinflation is a slowdown in the rate of inflation; prices still rise, only more slowly.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Correct: statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: The prefix 'dis' suggests a decline in prices, so disinflation is wrongly treated as deflation.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: The ozone layer that absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation is found in the:
explanation: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere, roughly 15 to 35 km above the Earth's surface.

optionReasoning.D: The exosphere is the outermost layer of the atmosphere.

misconception.text: Ground-level ozone is in the troposphere, which leads people to place the protective layer there.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Which of the following gases is the largest contributor to human-caused global warming?
explanation: Carbon dioxide released by burning fossil fuels and by deforestation is the largest contributor to human-caused warming. Nitrogen, oxygen and argon are not greenhouse gases.

optionReasoning.A: Nitrogen is the most abundant atmospheric gas but not a greenhouse gas.
optionReasoning.B: Oxygen is not a greenhouse gas.
optionReasoning.C: Argon is an inert gas and not a greenhouse gas.
optionReasoning.D: Carbon dioxide is the major anthropogenic greenhouse gas.

misconception.text: Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in the atmosphere, so people assume it is the main cause.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Jim Corbett National Park, India's oldest national park, is located in which State?
explanation: Jim Corbett National Park, established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, is in Uttarakhand.

optionReasoning.A: Corbett is in Uttarakhand.
optionReasoning.B: Assam hosts Kaziranga and Manas.
optionReasoning.C: Rajasthan hosts Ranthambore and Keoladeo.
optionReasoning.D: Karnataka hosts Bandipur and Nagarhole.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Kaziranga National Park is best known for the conservation of:
explanation: Kaziranga in Assam holds the largest population of the Indian one-horned rhinoceros. The Asiatic lion is found in Gir.

optionReasoning.A: The Asiatic lion lives in Gir National Park, Gujarat.
optionReasoning.B: The snow leopard lives in the high Himalayas.
optionReasoning.C: Kaziranga is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros.
optionReasoning.D: The Great Indian Bustard is found in dry grasslands of Rajasthan and Gujarat.

misconception.text: Gir is a famous Indian wildlife park, so lions are linked wrongly with Kaziranga.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: World Environment Day is observed every year on:
explanation: World Environment Day is observed on 5 June. Earth Day is on 22 April and World Water Day on 22 March.

optionReasoning.B: 22 March is World Water Day.
optionReasoning.C: 5 June is World Environment Day.

misconception.text: Earth Day is the better-known environmental observance.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: In an ecosystem, the primary producers are:
explanation: Green plants and other photosynthetic organisms are the primary producers, since they convert solar energy into chemical energy that supports other trophic levels.

optionReasoning.A: Herbivores are primary consumers.
optionReasoning.B: Decomposers break down dead matter.
optionReasoning.C: Carnivores are secondary or tertiary consumers.
optionReasoning.D: Green plants are the producers.

misconception.text: Decomposers make nutrients available again, so they are sometimes called producers.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Ramsar Convention. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Ramsar Convention regulates international trade in endangered species.
The Ramsar Convention is concerned with the conservation of wetlands.
explanation: The Ramsar Convention (1971) is on wetlands of international importance. International trade in endangered species is regulated by CITES.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Correct: statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: Both are international conventions on nature, so Ramsar is credited with CITES's subject as well.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Montreal Protocol and the Kyoto Protocol. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Montreal Protocol aims to phase out substances that deplete the ozone layer.
The Kyoto Protocol set emission reduction targets for greenhouse gases.
explanation: The Montreal Protocol (1987) controls ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs. The Kyoto Protocol (1997) set binding greenhouse gas reduction targets for developed countries.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Correct: both statements are correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: The Kyoto Protocol is thought to concern the ozone layer.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Which of the following regions of India is part of a global biodiversity hotspot?
explanation: The Western Ghats (with Sri Lanka) is one of the global biodiversity hotspots. India's other hotspots include the Himalaya, Indo-Burma and Sundaland (Nicobar).

optionReasoning.A: The Thar Desert is not a hotspot.
optionReasoning.B: The Western Ghats are a global biodiversity hotspot.
optionReasoning.C: The interior Deccan Plateau is not a hotspot.
optionReasoning.D: The Indo-Gangetic Plain is largely farmland.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Project Tiger was launched in India in:
explanation: Project Tiger was launched in April 1973 to protect the tiger and its habitat in specially created tiger reserves.

optionReasoning.C: 1980 is the year of the Forest (Conservation) Act.
optionReasoning.D: 1992 is the year of the Rio Earth Summit.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Acid rain is mainly caused by the atmospheric release of:

explanation: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides react with water vapour to form sulphuric and nitric acids, which fall as acid rain.

optionReasoning.B: Carbon monoxide and methane do not form strong acids in rain.
optionReasoning.C: CFCs deplete the ozone layer.
optionReasoning.D: Ozone and argon are not acid-forming.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Consider the following statements regarding energy flow in an ecosystem. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Wildlife (Protection) Act. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

explanation: The Wildlife (Protection) Act was enacted in 1972 and provides for protected areas; the Environment (Protection) Act dates from 1986.

optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Eutrophication of a lake is mainly caused by an excess of:
options: nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus
explanation: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus from fertilisers and sewage trigger algal blooms. When the algae die and decompose, dissolved oxygen falls and aquatic life suffers.

optionReasoning.A: Heavy metals cause toxicity but not algal blooms.
optionReasoning.B: Oil spills form a film but are not the cause of nutrient enrichment.
optionReasoning.C: Nutrient enrichment causes eutrophication.
optionReasoning.D: Heat discharge is thermal pollution.

misconception.text: Heavy metals are a leading water pollutant, so they are blamed for every lake problem.

subject: prelims-environment
stem: Consider the following statements regarding Rhizobium. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Rhizobium forms root nodules on cereal crops such as wheat.
Rhizobium bacteria are able to fix atmospheric nitrogen.
explanation: Rhizobium lives in root nodules of leguminous plants such as pulses and fixes atmospheric nitrogen. Cereals like wheat do not form such nodules.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.B: Correct: statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.

misconception.text: Nitrogen fixation is thought to benefit all crops equally, so nodules on wheat are accepted.

subject: prelims-science-technology
stem: Which vitamin is synthesised in the human skin on exposure to sunlight?
explanation: The skin synthesises vitamin D when exposed to ultraviolet-B radiation from the Sun.

optionReasoning.A: Vitamin A comes from foods such as carrots and liver.
optionReasoning.B: Vitamin D is synthesised in the skin.
optionReasoning.C: Vitamin C is obtained from citrus fruits and cannot be made by humans.
optionReasoning.D: Vitamin K is made by gut bacteria and found in green leafy vegetables.

misconception.text: Vitamin C is the best-known vitamin from fruit and is confused with sunlight.

subject: prelims-science-technology
stem: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
explanation: Mars appears red because of iron oxide on its surface.

optionReasoning.A: Venus is covered by thick clouds and appears bright white.
optionReasoning.B: Jupiter is a gas giant with banded clouds.
optionReasoning.C: Mercury is the planet nearest the Sun.
optionReasoning.D: Mars is called the Red Planet.

misconception.text: Venus is the brightest planet in the sky and is sometimes associated with colour.

subject: prelims-science-technology
stem: Which gas is the most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78 per cent of dry air; oxygen is about 21 per cent.

optionReasoning.A: Nitrogen is the most abundant gas.
optionReasoning.B: Oxygen is the second most abundant gas.
optionReasoning.C: Carbon dioxide is a trace gas.
optionReasoning.D: Argon is the third most abundant gas, at about 0.9 per cent.

misconception.text: Oxygen is the gas we depend on, so it is assumed to be the most abundant.

subject: prelims-science-technology
stem: The SI unit of electric current is:
explanation: The ampere is the SI unit of electric current. The volt measures potential difference, the ohm resistance and the watt power.

optionReasoning.A: The volt is the unit of potential difference.
optionReasoning.B: The ohm is the unit of resistance.
optionReasoning.C: The ampere is the unit of electric current.
optionReasoning.D: The watt is the unit of power.

misconception.text: Volt is the most familiar electrical unit, but it measures potential difference.

subject: prelims-science-technology
stem: Consider the following statements regarding sound and light. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Sound can travel through a vacuum.
Light cannot travel through a vacuum.
explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium, so it cannot travel through a vacuum. Light is an electromagnetic wave and travels through a vacuum, as sunlight reaches the Earth.

optionReasoning.A: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.B: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.D: Correct: neither statement is correct.

misconception.text: Sound and light are both called waves, so sound is assumed to cross a vacuum like light, and light to need a medium like sound.

subject: prelims-science-technology
stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's Moon and Mars missions. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Chandrayaan-3 made a soft landing near the lunar south polar region in 2023.
India's Mars Orbiter Mission made a soft landing on Mars.
explanation: Chandrayaan-3's lander touched down on 23 August 2023 in the Moon's south polar region. The Mars Orbiter Mission (2013) placed a spacecraft in orbit around Mars; it did not land.

optionReasoning.A: Correct: statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.B: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.

misconception.text: Entering Mars orbit is mistakenly taken as landing on it.

subject: prelims-science-technology
stem: Antibiotics are effective in treating infections caused by:
explanation: Antibiotics act on bacteria; they are not effective against viruses, which are treated with antivirals or prevented with vaccines.

optionReasoning.A: Antibiotics do not work against viruses.
optionReasoning.B: They are not effective against viruses.
optionReasoning.C: They are effective against bacteria.
optionReasoning.D: Antibiotics treat bacterial infections.

misconception.text: Antibiotics are used for colds and flu in practice, which does not make them effective against viruses.

subject: prelims-science-technology
stem: The sugar present in the DNA molecule is:
explanation: DNA contains deoxyribose. RNA contains ribose.

optionReasoning.A: Ribose is the sugar in RNA.
optionReasoning.B: Deoxyribose is the sugar in DNA.
optionReasoning.C: Glucose is a simple sugar used for energy.
optionReasoning.D: Fructose is a fruit sugar.

misconception.text: Ribose and deoxyribose differ by one oxygen atom, and the two nucleic acids are confused.

subject: prelims-science-technology
stem: Consider the following statements regarding optical fibres and total internal reflection. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Optical fibres transmit light signals by total internal reflection.
Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium.
explanation: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium at an angle larger than the critical angle. Optical fibres use it to keep light inside the core.

optionReasoning.A: Correct: statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.B: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.C: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
optionReasoning.D: Wrong: it claims statement 1 is incorrect and statement 2 is incorrect, but statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.

misconception.text: Both media are mentioned together, and the direction of travel is reversed.

subject: prelims-science-technology
stem: Isotopes of an element have:
options: the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons
the same mass number but different atomic numbers
different numbers of protons and electrons
explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element, which have the same atomic number (protons) but different mass numbers because of different neutron numbers.

optionReasoning.A: This defines isotopes.
optionReasoning.B: That describes isotones.
optionReasoning.C: That describes isobars.
optionReasoning.D: Atoms with different numbers of protons are different elements.

misconception.text: Isobars also share a property that is easily confused with isotopes.

subject: prelims-csat
stem: A train 120 metres long crosses a pole in 6 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
explanation: Speed = 120 m / 6 s = 20 m/s. Multiplying by 18/5 converts it to km/h: 20 x 3.6 = 72 km/h.

optionReasoning.A: 60 km/h would take 7.2 seconds to cover 120 m.
optionReasoning.B: 20 m/s equals 72 km/h.
optionReasoning.C: 80 km/h is about 22.2 m/s, which would take about 5.4 seconds.
optionReasoning.D: 90 km/h is 25 m/s, which would take 4.8 seconds.

misconception.text: Dividing 120 by 6 gives 20, and some then multiply by 3 instead of 3.6.

subject: prelims-csat
stem: If 40 per cent of a number is 60, what is the number?
explanation: If 40 per cent of x is 60, then x = 60 / 0.4 = 150.

optionReasoning.A: 40 per cent of 120 is 48.
optionReasoning.B: 40 per cent of 150 is 60.
optionReasoning.C: 40 per cent of 180 is 72.
optionReasoning.D: 40 per cent of 240 is 96.

misconception.text: Doubling 60 to get 120 looks natural, but it treats 40 per cent as one half.

subject: prelims-csat
stem: What is the average of 12, 15, 18, 21 and 24?
explanation: The sum is 12 + 15 + 18 + 21 + 24 = 90, and 90 / 5 = 18. The numbers are in arithmetic progression, so the average is the middle term.

optionReasoning.A: 16 would give a sum of 80.
optionReasoning.B: 17 would give a sum of 85.
optionReasoning.C: The sum is 90, so the average is 18.
optionReasoning.D: 19 would give a sum of 95.

misconception.text: Estimating the average from the lower terms alone gives a value such as 17, but for an arithmetic progression the average is the middle term, 18.

subject: prelims-csat
stem: A sum of 360 rupees is divided among three persons in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest share in rupees?
explanation: The ratio parts add up to 2 + 3 + 4 = 9, so one part is 360 / 9 = 40 rupees. The largest share is 4 x 40 = 160 rupees.

optionReasoning.A: 120 is the share for the ratio part 3.
optionReasoning.B: 140 does not correspond to any whole number of parts.
optionReasoning.C: The largest share is 4 x 40 = 160.
optionReasoning.D: 180 would be half of the total, which is more than 4/9 of 360.

misconception.text: 120 is the middle share (3 x 40), which is picked if the ratio parts are mixed up.

subject: prelims-csat
stem: A can complete a piece of work in 12 days and B can complete it in 18 days. Working together, in how many days will they complete it?
explanation: In one day A does 1/12 and B does 1/18 of the work, together 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36. They finish in 36/5 = 7.2 days.

optionReasoning.A: 6 days would need a combined rate of 1/6, which is more than 5/36.
optionReasoning.B: The combined rate is 5/36, so the work takes 7.2 days.
optionReasoning.C: 7.5 days would need a rate of 2/15, which is less than 5/36.
optionReasoning.D: 8 days would need a rate of 1/8, which is less than 5/36.

misconception.text: Averaging the two times gives 15, and half of 15 is 7.5.

subject: prelims-csat
stem: What is the simple interest on 5,000 rupees at 8 per cent per annum for 3 years?
explanation: Simple interest = principal x rate x time / 100 = 5,000 x 8 x 3 / 100 = 1,200 rupees.

optionReasoning.A: 800 rupees is the interest for 2 years, not 3.
optionReasoning.C: 1,250 rupees does not match the formula.
optionReasoning.D: 1,500 rupees would need a rate of 10 per cent.

misconception.text: Computing the interest for 2 years instead of 3 gives 800 rupees.

subject: prelims-csat
stem: A shopkeeper buys an article for 800 rupees and sells it at a profit of 20 per cent. What is the selling price?
explanation: Profit = 20 per cent of 800 = 160 rupees, so the selling price is 800 + 160 = 960 rupees.

optionReasoning.A: 920 rupees corresponds to a profit of 15 per cent.
optionReasoning.B: 940 rupees corresponds to a profit of 17.5 per cent.
optionReasoning.C: The selling price is 800 x 1.2 = 960.
optionReasoning.D: 980 rupees corresponds to a profit of 22.5 per cent.

misconception.text: Adding 120 instead of 160 corresponds to taking 15 per cent of 800 as the profit.

subject: prelims-csat
stem: Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. Conclusions: I. Some roses fade quickly. II. Some flowers are roses. Which of the conclusions follows from the statements?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
explanation: From 'All roses are flowers' we can conclude that some flowers are roses, so II follows. The flowers that fade quickly may not be roses, so I does not follow.

optionReasoning.A: I does not follow because the fading flowers need not include roses.
optionReasoning.B: I does not follow, so both cannot follow.
optionReasoning.C: Only II follows.
optionReasoning.D: II follows by conversion of the first statement.

misconception.text: Roses are a subset of flowers, so it is assumed that the fast-fading flowers include roses.

subject: prelims-csat
stem: A man travels 60 km at a speed of 30 km/h and returns along the same route at 20 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
explanation: Time going = 60 / 30 = 2 hours; time returning = 60 / 20 = 3 hours. Total distance 120 km in 5 hours gives 120 / 5 = 24 km/h.

optionReasoning.A: Total distance 120 km / total time 5 h = 24 km/h.
optionReasoning.B: 25 km/h is the simple mean of 30 and 20, which is wrong when distances are equal.
optionReasoning.C: 26 km/h does not follow from the data.
optionReasoning.D: 27.5 km/h does not follow from the data.

misconception.text: The simple average of the speeds is 25, but equal distances need the harmonic mean.

subject: prelims-csat
stem: A 40-litre mixture of milk and water contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much water must be added so that the ratio of milk to water becomes 3 : 2?
explanation: The mixture has 30 litres of milk and 10 litres of water. For a ratio of 3 : 2 the water must be 20 litres, so 10 litres have to be added.

optionReasoning.A: Adding 5 litres gives 30 : 15, which is 2 : 1.
optionReasoning.B: Adding 10 litres gives 30 : 20, which is 3 : 2.
optionReasoning.C: Adding 15 litres gives 30 : 25, which is 6 : 5.
optionReasoning.D: Adding 20 litres gives 30 : 30, which is 1 : 1.

misconception.text: Doubling the original 10 litres of water to 20 is mistaken for the amount to add.
